mode_evidence: The object is a retinal after-image (red dot) seen with closed eyes, then the murk and colour fields in the visual field; Stein reports stunning colours, crab-like creatures seen even with eyes open, and light shot from a fingertip into the night sky, while Ingram notes another meditator saw the colours of a pentagram drawn in daylight. The nimitta glossary entry calls it a 'mind-created disk', but the testimony is of seen colour.
onset_evidence: Induction is the opening instruction: stare at the flame a minute or two, close eyes, follow the after-image, repeat. Sequence then red dot, murk, colours; patience is required and 'something will organise out of that'. Beginners whose dots shift or fade are told to keep patiently returning attention to whatever is in the field. Ingram also reports doing it 'cold' with only eyelid colours and a white kasina. No cannot-be-forced statement; time scale: Stein reached second-jhana red dot within hours of starting, brilliant colour by day nine of 25.

conditions.gaze_or_eye_position: Stare at flame three to five feet away; then eyes closed on the after-image; later eyes open in dim rooms.
conditions.setting: Still air or a glass frame round the flame; dawn, dusk and night best for eyes-open images; keep rooms dark early on.
conditions.duration_and_schedule: Look a minute or two, close eyes, follow the image until static, repeat endlessly; retreat context of 25 days with hours of sitting.
conditions.prerequisites: Strong concentration helps; Ingram had done vipassana for days first.
conditions.other: A low-power LED can refresh the after-image between sits.

stages.label: red dot
stages.description: Closed-eye after-image of the flame, the object to follow.

stages.label: dissolution / murk
stages.description: Dot dissolves into a vague field; where attention drifts and progress is made.

stages.label: colour with depth
stages.description: Airy colours gain 3D depth, then smooth pools of blue and green, then brilliant colour; later moving scenes and radial symmetry patterns ('rainbow flux lines').

what_to_do_with_light: Give full attention to the after-image, favouring anything like a red dot; follow it until static, then refresh by looking again. Carry it off the cushion and into eyes-open walking, keep extending it into daylight; notice the luminosity of the murk.
obstacles_and_fixes: Dissolution phase with spacing out: keep attending; use light exercise and movement.
Image too faint in light rooms: stay in dimmer rooms or refresh with an LED.
Shifting faint dots early: patiently return attention to whatever is in the field.
Fear stage with creatures: back off and rest.
cautions: Candle safety: clear combustibles and extinguish after each sit.
Fear stage and strange visions can be alarming on solo retreat; have a guide.
interpretation: The after-image and nimitta are the object of kasina concentration, mapped onto the jhanas, with the visuals used as a diagram of what attention does across states.
practice_summary: Sit three to five feet from a steady candle flame. Stare at it for a minute or two, until it looks strange or purplish. Close your eyes and give full attention to the after-image, especially any red dot. Follow it for as long as it lasts, until only static remains; then open your eyes, look at the flame again, close them, and repeat many times. When the dot dissolves, keep attending to the murk and to its luminosity, giving it a minute or two, and organisation will emerge: colours, depth, then moving imagery. Be patient. Carry the image off the cushion with eyes half open in dim rooms, refreshing with an LED if necessary, and stretch eyes-open images toward daylight.

key_passages.anchor: Sit comfortably and stare at the flame for a minute or two or until things start feeling they are getting a little
key_passages.paraphrase: Stare at the flame until the visual field turns strange or purplish, then close your eyes.

key_passages.anchor: Then close your eyes and stare at the after-images that come, and if you see anything resembling a red dot give that more attention.
key_passages.paraphrase: Take the closed-eye after-image as the object, favouring a red dot.

key_passages.anchor: Follow it for as long as it endures until you have just static, then open your eyes and look at the flame again.
key_passages.paraphrase: Cycle between looking and following until nothing organised remains, then give the remainder another minute or two.

key_passages.locator: Day Eight eyes-open practice, source lines 2947-3045
key_passages.anchor: as you progress, keep extending the eyes-open images out into the day
key_passages.paraphrase: Maintain the stable image while moving with eyes open, at night and dawn first, then into daylight.

key_passages.anchor: Then the murk, which at times can be quite dark, is much easier to transition through when I notice the luminosity.
key_passages.paraphrase: Stein's reported sequence: red dot, shapes at its edges, murk, then airy colours with depth.
